text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.82% today, continuing a sharp two-week decline of 9.26%. The immediate pressure came from oil prices edging lower on Thursday as U.S.-Iran peace negotiations eased supply concerns in the Middle East—crude fell from the $123 range to $103 per barrel. For a refiner, lower oil prices can pinch profit margins on fuel production, especially when crude drops this sharply, even though refineries are running at a healthy 92.8% capacity.

The broader headwind is that Big Oil earnings season is arriving with investor caution around guidance; refiners depend on sustained margins and refining spreads that tighten when crude prices fall this quickly. The recent geopolitical volatility that had supported higher oil prices (and wider refining profits) is now reversing as peace talks reduce urgency, leaving the stock caught between uncertainty over how long margins will hold and a market that's already pricing in skepticism about what companies will project ahead.
